text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Thousands of faithful and seekers of healing miracles on Monday converged at a Blantyre stadium to hear German evangelist Reinhard Bonnke preach and pray for the sick during his week-long 'Gospel for All Crusade' organised by Charismatic and Pentecotal Association of Malawi.

- Customs department alarmed by successes of drug barons in beating the country's police checks in the borders and airports have decided to join the war against drug-trafficking, head of investigation Jim Barnard said on Wednesday.

- A mother of five who decided to stop giving birth to more children and underwent a tubular legation, an operation to cut fallopian tubes, has sued the family planning organisation, Banja La Mtsogolo, after she ended up with another pregnancy 18 months later.

- The ruling United Democratic Front party Secretary General Sam Mpasu on Wednesday accused former presidential economic advisor Kalonga Stambuli of harbouring political intentions to undermine government using the "opposition newspapers" to bring down the democratically elected government.

- The Teachers Union of Malawi is expected to meet on Friday to plan the next form of action following empty promises by Education Ministry which has not paid monthly salaries to some teachers since January this year.
